entries.subject: A false color from three measured bands, as the HR 8799 planets have
entries.finding: Shown in infrared false color from its measured flux in MKO K 2.184 µm, MKO H 1.614 µm, MKO J 1.2417 µm (Ward et al. (2021), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). No paper checked gives flux densities of this companion in three JWST bands like the NIRCam F410M, F430M and F460M that color HR 8799's planets. Its color is from ground-based J, H and K photometry on its own range, so it is not compared with theirs.
entries.revisitWhen: Flux densities in three bands comparable with HR 8799's are published.

entries.subject: A candidate moon, HD 206893 B I
entries.finding: Kral et al. (2026) find tentative residuals in B's GRAVITY positions that a moon of about 0.4 Jupiter masses on a 0.76-year orbit would explain, but say they could be systematic errors. No moon is drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: Further GRAVITY astrometry confirms or rules out the signal.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law fitted to the MKO H intensity PICASO 4.1 (Batalha et al. 2019, ApJ 878, 70) computes from Exo-REM cloudy (Charnay et al. 2018, ApJ 854, 172; 1 times solar metallicity, C/O 0.75) model atmospheres at 1,347 K and log g 3.55, read between the models YGP_1300K_logg3.5, YGP_1300K_logg4.0, YGP_1350K_logg3.5, YGP_1350K_logg4.0 (u1 0.656, u2 0.043; the law fits each model's eight angles within 0.10% of the centre): a cloudy model, the one Kammerer et al. (2021), arXiv:2106.08249 fit to this planet, because no table reaches a planet this cold and nobody has resolved its disc. The temperature and gravity are that fit's (Table 6, Exo-REM with extinction by enstatite dust (the dusty model): Teff 1347 +6/-7 K, log g 3.55 +0.06/-0.04 (toward the grid's lower boundary), [Fe/H] 0.06 +0.09/-0.07, C/O 0.75 +0.00/-0.01 (toward the upper boundary), radius 2.03 +/- 0.08, A_V 2.87 +0.36/-0.30, reduced chi-squared 0.757; the plain Exo-REM fit (1049 K, radius 2.32) is the one the paper calls an outlier; [record](source/photometry/atmosphere-fit.json)), not the 1,162 K of its measurements record. The paper dims this model by the extinction of enstatite dust, applied to the whole disc alike; the law is the model atmosphere's, without that dust.
